author: Aulus Hirtius
work: De Bello Gallico, liber VIII (auctore Hirtio)

pairs.source_text: Caesaris nostri commentarios rerum gestarum Galliae, non comparantibus superioribus atque insequentibus eius scriptis, contexui novissimumque imperfectum ab rebus gestis Alexandriae confeci usque ad exitum non quidem civilis dissensionis, cuius finem nullum videmus, sed vitae Caesaris.
pairs.question: Quis octavum De Bello Gallico librum scripsit, ut Caesaris commentarios imperfectos conficeret?
pairs.question_en: Who wrote the eighth book of De Bello Gallico, in order to complete Caesar's unfinished commentaries?
pairs.derivation: Authorship fact: Book 8 is not by Caesar but by his officer Aulus Hirtius, who in the preface (first person, 'contexui ... confeci') states he wove together and completed Caesar's unfinished Commentarii on the Gallic War. The author's identity (Hirtius) is the manuscript heading and a standard fact of literary history; the substance (a continuator completed the imperfect last commentary) is verbatim in the source. Closed-book, entity-anchored to the eighth book and Caesar's commentaries.

pairs.source_text: Coactus assiduis tuis vocibus, Balbe, cum cotidiana mea recusatio non difficultatis excusationem, sed inertiae videretur deprecationem habere, rem difficillimam suscepi.
pairs.question: Quem Hirtius in prooemio octavi De Bello Gallico libri alloquitur?
pairs.question_en: Whom does Hirtius address in the preface of the eighth book of De Bello Gallico?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Hirtius's preface; the addressee is named in the vocative 'Balbe' (Cornelius Balbus, Caesar's confidant), supported verbatim. Single named answer; closed-book detail of literary history.

pairs.source_text: Ibi cum Lucterius apud suos cives quondam integris rebus multum potuisset, semperque auctor novorum consiliorum magnam apud barbaros auctoritatem haberet, oppidum Uxellodunum, quod in clientela fuerat eius, egregie natura loci munitum, occupat suis et Drappetis copiis oppidanosque sibi coniungit.
pairs.question: Quod oppidum Lucterius et Drappes copiis suis occupaverunt, ubi ultima Gallorum defensio facta est?
pairs.question_en: Which town did Lucterius and Drappes seize with their forces, where the last Gallic resistance was made?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Lucterius and Drappes; the town Uxellodunum supported verbatim ('oppidum Uxellodunum ... occupat suis et Drappetis copiis'). Uxellodunum, the last great stronghold of Gallic resistance, is closed-book; single named answer.

pairs.source_text: Cum contra exspectationem omnium Caesar Uxellodunum venisset oppidumque operibus clausum animadverteret neque ab oppugnatione recedi videret ulla condicione posse, magna autem copia frumenti abundare oppidanos ex perfugis cognosset, aqua prohibere hostem temptare coepit.
pairs.question: Cum oppidani Uxelloduni frumento abundarent, qua re Caesar eos ad deditionem coegit?
pairs.question_en: Since the townsmen of Uxellodunum had abundant grain, by what means did Caesar force them to surrender?
pairs.answer_en: By cutting off their water supply.
pairs.derivation: Method fact anchored to Caesar and Uxellodunum; since the town had ample grain, Caesar cut off its water ('aqua prohibere hostem temptare coepit'), supported verbatim. The water-deprivation of Uxellodunum is the defining feature of the siege; closed-book, short answer.

pairs.source_text: Itaque omnibus qui arma tulerant manus praecidit vitamque concessit, quo testatior esset poena improborum.
pairs.question: Quam poenam Caesar Uxelloduno capto eis qui arma tulerant inflixit?
pairs.question_en: What punishment did Caesar inflict on those who had borne arms when Uxellodunum was captured?
pairs.derivation: Distinctive event fact anchored to Caesar and the captured Uxellodunum; 'omnibus qui arma tulerant manus praecidit vitamque concessit' supported verbatim — he cut off the hands of all who had borne arms but spared their lives, as a deterrent. A notorious episode of the campaign; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: unaque consilium cum eo Lucterium Cadurcum cepisse, quem superiore commentario prima defectione Galliae facere in provinciam voluisse impetum cognitum est
pairs.question: Cuius gentis fuit Lucterius, qui cum Drappete Uxellodunum tenuit?
pairs.question_en: Of what people was Lucterius, who held Uxellodunum together with Drappes?
pairs.derivation: Ethnicity fact anchored to Lucterius; 'Lucterium Cadurcum' supported verbatim. Lucterius the Cadurcan, a leader of the final revolt and of the Uxellodunum holdout, is closed-book; single short answer.

pairs.source_text: Qua ex fuga cum constaret Drappetem Senonem, qui, ut primum defecerat Gallia, collectis undique perditis hominibus, servis ad libertatem vocatis, exulibus omnium civitatum adscitis, receptis latronibus impedimenta et commeatus Romanorum interceperat, non amplius hominum duobus milibus ex fuga collectis provinciam petere
pairs.question: Cuius gentis fuit Drappes, socius Lucterii apud Uxellodunum?
pairs.question_en: Of what people was Drappes, Lucterius's ally at Uxellodunum?
pairs.derivation: Ethnicity fact anchored to Drappes; 'Drappetem Senonem' supported verbatim. Drappes the Senonian, who with Lucterius held Uxellodunum, is entity-anchored and verifiable; single short answer.

pairs.source_text: Eodem tempore Lacterius, quem profugisse ex proelio scripsi, cum in potestatem venisset Epasnacti Arverni (crebro enim mutandis locis multorum fidei se committebat, quod nusquam diutius sine periculo commoraturus videbatur, cum sibi conscius esset, quam inimicum deberet Caesarem habere), hunc Epasnactus Arvernus, amicissimus populi Romani, sine dubitatione ulla vinctum ad Caesarem deduxit.
pairs.question: Quis Arvernus, amicus populi Romani, Lucterium vinctum ad Caesarem deduxit?
pairs.question_en: Which Arvernian, a friend of the Roman people, brought Lucterius in chains to Caesar?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Lucterius; 'Epasnactus Arvernus, amicissimus populi Romani, ... vinctum ad Caesarem deduxit' supported verbatim. Epasnactus the Arvernian handed Lucterius over to Caesar. Note the text spells the name here as 'Lacterius' (i.e. Lucterius). Entity-anchored; single named answer.

pairs.source_text: Bellovacos, qui belli gloria Gallos omnes Belgasque praestabant, finitimasque his civitates duce Correo Bellovaco et Commio Atrebate exercitus comparare atque in unum locum cogere, ut omni multitudine in fines Suessionum, qui Remis erant attributi, facerent impressionem
pairs.question: Quibus ducibus Bellovaci finitimaeque civitates contra Romanos arma comparaverunt?
pairs.question_en: Under what leaders did the Bellovaci and neighboring states raise arms against the Romans?
pairs.answer_en: Under Correus the Bellovacan and Commius the Atrebatian.
pairs.derivation: Leaders fact anchored to the Bellovaci; the two named leaders 'duce Correo Bellovaco et Commio Atrebate' supported verbatim. Correus the Bellovacan and Commius the Atrebatian, heads of the Belgic revolt, are entity-anchored; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Commius incensum calcaribus equum coniungit equo Quadrati lanceaque infesta magnis viribus medium femur traicit Voluseni.
pairs.question: Quem Commius Atrebas lancea per medium femur vulneravit?
pairs.question_en: Whom did Commius the Atrebatian wound with a lance through the middle of the thigh?
pairs.derivation: Name/event fact anchored to Commius the Atrebatian; 'lanceaque infesta ... medium femur traicit Voluseni' supported verbatim. Commius wounded the cavalry prefect Gaius Volusenus Quadratus in the thigh; entity-anchored, single named answer; closed-book episode of Commius's feud with the Romans.

pairs.source_text: Cum in Carnutes venisset, quorum in civitate superiore commentario Caesar exposuit initium belli esse ortum, quod praecipue eos propter conscientiam facti timere animadvertebat, quo celerius civitatem timore liberaret, principem sceleris illius et concitatorem belli, Gutruatum, ad supplicium depoposcit.
pairs.question: Quem virum Caesar apud Carnutes, ut belli concitatorem, ad supplicium depoposcit?
pairs.question_en: Which man did Caesar demand for execution among the Carnutes as the rouser of the war?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to the Carnutes and Caesar; 'concitatorem belli, Gutruatum, ad supplicium depoposcit' supported verbatim. Gutruatus, the instigator of the Carnutian revolt that began the war, was handed over and put to death; entity-anchored, single named answer.

pairs.source_text: Scio Caesarem singulorum annorum singulos commentarios confecisse; quod ego non existimavi mihi esse faciendum, propterea quod insequens annus, L. Paulo C. Marcello consulibus, nullas habet magnopere Galliae res gestas.
pairs.question: Quibus consulibus fuit insequens annus, quo, ut Hirtius scribit, nullae magnae in Gallia res gestae sunt?
pairs.question_en: In whose consulship was the following year, in which, as Hirtius writes, no great deeds were done in Gaul?
pairs.derivation: Date/office fact anchored to Hirtius's authorial note; the consuls L. Aemilius Paulus and C. Claudius Marcellus (50 BC) supported verbatim. Also records Hirtius's remark that, unlike Caesar (one commentary per year), he combined the quiet year. Closed-book Roman fasti; named answer.

pairs.source_text: Labienus interim in Treveris equestre proelium facit secundum compluribusque Treveris interfectis et Germanis, qui nullis adversus Romanos auxilia denegabant, principes eorum vivos redigit in suam potestatem atque in his Surum Aeduum, qui et virtutis et generis summam nobilitatem habebat solusque ex Aeduis ad id tempus permanserat in armis.
pairs.question: Quis solus ex Aeduis ad id tempus in armis permanserat, qui a Labieno captus est?
pairs.question_en: Who alone of the Aedui had up to that time remained in arms, and was captured by Labienus?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to the Aedui and Labienus; 'Surum Aeduum ... solusque ex Aeduis ad id tempus permanserat in armis' supported verbatim. Surus, the last Aeduan still in arms, captured by Labienus among the Treveri; entity-anchored, single named answer.
